analysis.title: Extreme fear, record panic hedging, dare to buy
key_insights: Friday's VIX and VVIX spike showed forced deleveraging and panic hedging, with traders buying tail protection at almost any price.
SDEX and TDEX (tail-risk hedging demand gauges) rose more than VIX, showing the strongest demand for protection against a major downside shock.
Per GS's Lee Coppersmith, Friday was the first real sign of panic in index hedging, after weeks of damage beneath the surface and in client portfolios.
VIX futures volume reached 3.6x its 20-day average, Cboe index put volume hit an all-time high, and total put volume was the fourth-highest since 2015.
VIX call volume was the second-highest in five years, behind only August 2, 2024, which preceded VIX rising above 60 the following Monday.
The VIX spike was large relative to the SPX decline. Since 1990, only nine other sessions had a larger VIX spike with a smaller SPX decline (SpotGamma).
Equity volatility had ignored stress in credit markets. Friday narrowed the gap with CDX IG, though the divergence remains wide.
Dealer gamma fell by a reported $5.9bn on Friday, leaving aggregate positioning near neutral. Monthly expiration likely contributed.
With the dealer gamma cushion fading, volatility could spread from individual stocks to the index.
CNN's Fear & Greed gauge is back in extreme fear but below the April panic levels. Buying extreme fear has historically been profitable, and the note asks whether readers will do so this time.
risk_factors: Fading positive dealer gamma could let single-stock and sector volatility spread to the index.
Credit stress as measured by CDX IG remains wide relative to VIX.
The August 2, 2024 precedent: a similar VIX call volume surge was followed by VIX rising above 60 the next Monday.
vol_and_positioning: VIX and VVIX spiked on Friday in what the note calls forced deleveraging and panic hedging.
SDEX and TDEX moved more than VIX, showing extreme demand for tail protection.
VIX futures volume was 3.6x its 20-day average. Cboe index put volume was an all-time high. Total put volume was the fourth-highest since 2015 (GS).
VIX call volume was the second-highest in five years, behind only August 2, 2024 (GS/Bloomberg).
Only nine sessions since 1990 had a larger VIX spike alongside a smaller SPX decline. VIX is typically about 5x as volatile as SPX (SpotGamma).
Dealer gamma fell by $5.9bn on Friday, leaving aggregate positioning close to neutral (GS/Squeeze metrics).
Equity vol had lagged credit stress, and the divergence with CDX IG remains wide.

tension_points.bear_case: Dealer gamma has faded to near neutral, which could spread volatility from single stocks to the index, and equity vol is still well below credit stress signals.

theme_stances.evidence: This was panic hedging, not ordinary volatility buying.
